info.description: Answers assessment questionnaires from your guidelines and previously answered assessments.

Never 401s: the interface asks this on load to decide whether to show a
sign-in screen, and an error response would make "signed out" look like a
fault.

get.description:
The team's products, and whether the caller may change them.

`deleted` are the products deleted since plan 027, by name and colour: the
pages label the questionnaires and chats kept, read-only, from each.

schema.title: Response List Products Api Products Get

post.description: Add a product to the team. Its leads and administrators only.

schema.title: Response Add Product Api Products Post

schema.title: Response Edit Product Api Products  Product Id  Patch

delete.description:
Delete a product, with its documents and their files, and its remembered answers. Needs `confirm=confirm`.

The remembered answers include those moved in from the shared memory. Its
questionnaires and chats are kept, read-only (plan 027). `removed` says how many of each.

schema.title: Response Delete Product Api Products  Product Id  Delete

get.description:
What deleting a product would remove, counted, for the page's warning. Changes nothing.

Its team's leads and administrators only, as deleting it is.

schema.title: Response Preview Deletion Api Products  Product Id  Deletion Get

get.description:
A deep link to the access panel, which lives inside the app itself.

The same document as `/`, because a deployment may only expose the
application's own address — an administrator who cannot reach a second URL
would otherwise have no way in. Nothing is protected by living at a separate
path anyway: `/api/admin/*` is what checks the role, and it does so whatever
page the request came from. This route exists only so the link still works
where that path *is* reachable.

Every column beside the questions, with its heading, for a person to choose where answers go (plan 043).

`GET /columns` is where they go now; this is what else there is. Choosing is `POST /columns`.

schema.title: Response Every Column Api Forms  Batch Id  Columns Every Get

post.description:
Read an uploaded questionnaire, for a `product` or General, and report what can be answered in it.

Nothing is answered here. The point of the separation is that a person sees
which sheets were used, which were skipped and why, and what each column was
taken to be, *before* a run that costs minutes.

`if_already_open="ask"`: when this person already has questionnaires read
from a file with exactly these bytes, nothing is saved, read or created,
and the answer is `{"already_open": [...]}`, last changed first, for them to
open one or start fresh (plan 029, 1.2). "new", the default, opens a new
questionnaire whatever there is, as it always did.

schema.title: Response Open Questionnaire Api Forms Post

get.description: One person's questionnaires, most recently used first, each with the day it is kept until (plan 033).

schema.title: Response List Questionnaires Api Forms Get

post.description:
Keep typed questions, or a PDF's or a Word file's, as a questionnaire with no file to write into (plan 033).

Multipart: one `questions` field per typed question, in order, and/or a
`file` (PDF or Word) whose questions are read first. `product` as for a
file, checked before anything is kept; `name` is what it is listed as (the
file's name, or "Typed questions", when left out). Nothing is answered:
the answer is the questionnaire as `GET /api/forms/{id}` returns it, with
`format` "list". 400 `no_questions_given` when there is nothing to keep;
422 `no_questions_found` when the file has no questions.

schema.title: Response Open Question List Api Forms List Post

get.description: One questionnaire. Opening it is using it: its `kept_until` starts again from now (plan 033).

schema.title: Response Get Questionnaire Api Forms  Batch Id  Get

delete.description:
Delete one of the caller's questionnaires, a list's or a deleted product's too, with its answers and files.

409 `questionnaire_busy` while it is being answered, or while a chat turn
runs in a conversation about it. A conversation about it still opens,
without its answers.

schema.title: Response Delete Questionnaire Api Forms  Batch Id  Delete

post.description:
Answer a selection. Long: a large questionnaire is minutes of work.

`/api/assessments/progress/{batch_id}` reports how far it has got while this
request is still open — the batch id is the run id, so it can be watched
from the moment the call is made.

schema.title: Response Answer Questionnaire Api Forms  Batch Id  Answer Post
Response Revise Questionnaire Api Forms  Batch Id  Revise Post
Response Write Answer By Hand Api Forms  Batch Id  Answers Post

post.description:
Leave a question deliberately blank rather than unanswered, or undo that.

The id travels in the body rather than the path: a question's id is the
file's own -- `Human Resources!4` -- and a sheet name may contain anything
a spreadsheet allows, slashes included.

schema.title: Response Leave An Answer Blank Api Forms  Batch Id  Blank Post

get.description: Which column each sheet's answers go into, and why detection thinks so.

schema.title: Response Get Column Roles Api Forms  Batch Id  Columns Get

post.description: Move a sheet's answers to a different column, or stop writing one.

schema.title: Response Set Column Role Api Forms  Batch Id  Columns Post

patch.description: Set questions aside, bring them back, or correct their wording.

schema.title: Response Correct Questions Api Forms  Batch Id  Questions Patch

post.description:
Switch a questionnaire between full and brief answers.

Switching to brief derives the short form of every answer that does not
have one yet -- one rewrite each, once. Switching back is instant, because
the full answer was never replaced: both are stored against the question and
the choice only says which one `fill` writes.

schema.title: Response Choose Answer Length Api Forms  Batch Id  Detail Post

post.description:
Refused unless it is the questionnaire's own product: a product is fixed when the file is opened.

Another product is 409 `product_locked` (TD-040); another team's is 404 `product_not_found` first.

schema.title: Response Choose Questionnaire Product Api Forms  Batch Id  Product Post

post.description: Write this one answer full or brief, whatever the rest of the file does.

schema.title: Response Choose One Answer Length Api Forms  Batch Id  Answers Length Post

post.description:
Release one answer for writing, with the reviewer's name on it.

Approving an answer somebody *wrote* also teaches the answer memory, which
is where the team's own answers come from once the imported questionnaires
run out; approving a draft nobody changed teaches it nothing, and
`remembered` comes back empty. The sweep for what a new entry supersedes or
contradicts runs after the response: it is model calls, and a reviewer
clicking through twenty answers should not wait for any of them.

schema.title: Response Approve An Answer Api Forms  Batch Id  Approve Post

post.description:
Release these held-back answers for writing, with the reviewer's name on them (plan 041).

Nothing goes into the answer memory, whoever wrote the words. The ids are
the ones the confirmation counted, so an answer that changed since then is
not swept up. `approved` lists the ids that were.

schema.title: Response Approve All Api Forms  Batch Id  Approve All Post

post.description: Write the confirmed answers into a copy of the original, and report the rest.

schema.title: Response Fill Questionnaire Api Forms  Batch Id  Fill Post

get.description: The filled copy. Produced by `/fill`, which must have run first.
The team's answered runs, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Runs Api Runs Get

get.description:
One run with its answers.

Scoped to the caller's team, so an id belonging to another team reads as
absent rather than forbidden.

schema.title: Response Get Run Api Runs  Run Id  Get

get.description: Recent activity for the team.

schema.title: Response List Events Api Events Get

get.description: What is currently indexed for the caller's team, shared or for one `product`.

schema.title: Response Get Knowledge Api Knowledge Get

delete.description:
Remove every policy document, shared or a `product`'s (with their files). The answer memory stays.

`files_left` names a product's files that could not be removed from the server.

schema.title: Response Clear Knowledge Api Knowledge Delete

post.description:
Index policy and guideline documents.

`authority` is "ours" for something this organisation wrote and is bound by,
"external" for a law, regulation or framework it is subject to. The drafter
is told which, because our policy says what we *do* and a regulation says
what we are *required* to do -- and answering the second as though it were
the first claims a control we may not have.

schema.title: Response Upload Guidelines Api Knowledge Guidelines Post

delete.description:
Remove one indexed policy document, from the shared knowledge base or a `product`'s (with its file).

`files_left` names a product's file that could not be removed from the server.

schema.title: Response Remove Source Api Knowledge Sources  Source Name  Delete

get.description: What we have said before, newest first: the shared memory, or a `product`'s.

schema.title: Response List Memory Api Memory Get

post.description: Teach the memory an answer by hand.

schema.title: Response Add Memory Entry Api Memory Post

get.description: Pairs that disagree, with both answers, for somebody to decide between. One memory's.

schema.title: Response List Memory Conflicts Api Memory Conflicts Get

patch.description:
Correct an entry. Not a supersession: nothing changed its mind.

A corrected answer is compared again, because correcting one is one of the
ways it comes to contradict another.

schema.title: Response Edit Memory Entry Api Memory  Entry Id  Patch

delete.description: Forget an entry: the row, its vector, and the conflicts it raised.

schema.title: Response Remove Memory Entry Api Memory  Entry Id  Delete

post.description: Put a superseded entry back into use, when the later answer was wrong.

schema.title: Response Restore Memory Entry Api Memory  Entry Id  Restore Post

post.description: Move an entry to the shared memory (`product` empty) or a product's, and compare it again there.

schema.title: Response Move Memory Entry Api Memory  Entry Id  Move Post

post.description: Say which of two disagreeing answers is our position, or that neither loses.

schema.title: Response Resolve Memory Conflict Api Memory Conflicts Resolve Post

post.description:
Compare everything that has arrived since the last sweep, and report it.

The same sweep that runs by itself after an upload or an approval, exposed
so a person can ask for it — after importing eleven questionnaires at once,
"has anything I just added contradicted us" is a question with an answer,
and waiting for a background task to have got round to it is not one.

Bounded, and it says how much is left. A sweep is one model call per entry
and a backlog can be hundreds: a button that returns in twenty seconds
saying what it found and what remains is a button somebody will press again,
and one that hangs for four minutes is one they will reload the page on.

schema.title: Response Scan Memory Now Api Memory Scan Post

get.description: Preferences, what they add up to, and every skill this person can use.

schema.title: Response Get Preferences Api Preferences Get
Response Save Preferences Api Preferences Put

post.description:
What a set of choices would tell the rewrite, without saving them.

So the page can show the instruction as the choices change, and try it on a
sample, from the one place that assembles it -- a copy of that logic in the
browser would drift from the one that actually runs.

schema.title: Response Compose Preferences Api Preferences Compose Post

post.description:
What an instruction does to one answer, before it is let loose on all of them.

Preferences are applied to every answer somebody drafts and a skill to a
whole selection, so a badly worded one reaches a questionnaire at once.
This is the same rewrite over one sample, stored nowhere, so the person sees
the effect first.

schema.title: Response Try A Style Api Preferences Try Post
Response Add Skill Api Skills Post
Response Edit Skill Api Skills  Skill Id  Patch
Response Remove Skill Api Skills  Skill Id  Delete

schema.title: Response Put Back The Draft Api Forms  Batch Id  Answers Draft Post

get.description:
Search the indexed corpus directly.

Separate from answering: this is for a person checking what the corpus
actually says, so it returns the chunks that matched rather than an answer
written from them. With a `product`, its knowledge base is searched too, and
the team's earlier answers have a share of the results (TD-074).

schema.title: Response Search Knowledge Api Search Get

get.description: The documents somebody has uploaded, for the interface to open.

schema.title: Response Get Documents Api Documents Get

get.description: Open or download the original PDF/DOCX document.
Return a browser preview: the original PDF or safe HTML converted from DOCX.
Extract and return the document text, using the persistent extraction cache.

schema.title: Response View Extracted Text Api Documents  Origin   Category   Name  Text Get

post.description:
Answer a new assessment.

`language` forces the output language ("ar" or "en"); omit it to answer each
question in the language it was asked.

`run_id` is chosen by the caller so it can watch the run while this request
is still open — answering a long assessment is minutes of silence, and the
identifier has to be known before the work starts to be of any use.

`product` answers it from that product's knowledge base beside the shared one.

Pull the questions out of an assessment without answering them.

The first half of `/answer`, separated so the questions can be reviewed and
corrected before a run that costs minutes. Extraction is the step most
likely to need a human eye: a numbered list can lose an item to a page
break, and a row of guidance can read as a question.

schema.title: Response Extract Assessment Api Assessments Extract Post

post.description:
Answer a list of questions supplied directly, with no document involved.

Serves three cases the document endpoint cannot: questions typed by hand,
questions extracted from a file and then corrected, and a second batch
added once an earlier one has been answered. The caller keeps the answers
and decides how to merge them, so this returns only what it was asked for.

Reword answers the caller is holding, with no questionnaire behind them.

The batch route does this for a file, keyed to the cells the answers belong
in. Questions typed by hand have no cells and no batch, so the answers come
in and go back out; the caller keeps them, exactly as it does for
`/answer-questions`. Both routes run the same rewrite, so an instruction
behaves the same whichever list it is given.

schema.title: Response Revise Answer List Api Assessments Revise Post

get.description: How far a run has got: questions found, answered, and left to answer.

schema.title: Response Assessment Progress Api Assessments Progress  Run Id  Get

post.description:
Render an answered assessment as a PDF.

The result is posted back rather than looked up, because the interface lets
a reviewer edit answers before exporting and those edits are the point.

By default the file carries only answers that were not flagged for review:
what goes back to an assessor should not silently include drafts the system
itself was unsure of.

Render an answered assessment as a Word document.

Same selection rule and same options as the PDF export; the difference is
that the reviewer can carry on editing in the file. Arabic is laid out by
Word rather than by us, which makes this the better format for an Arabic
questionnaire.

get.description:
The caller's own conversations, most recently used first, each with its product.

And with the turn running in it, or null (plan 031): the page marks the row,
and finds a new chat's id by the run id it sent the first message with. And
with the day it is kept until, or null when nothing is deleted (plan 033).

schema.title: Response List Conversations Api Chat Get

post.description:
One exchange with the assistant.

Long: a message can mean "answer 183 questions", which is minutes of work.
The conversation is saved by the assistant itself before this returns, so a
request that times out at a proxy has still recorded what it did. Meanwhile
it is held (`chat_running`): 409 `conversation_busy` for another message.

schema.title: Response Say To Assistant Api Chat Post

post.description:
A message with a questionnaire attached.

Separate from the plain message route because it is multipart, not because
it does anything different: the file is saved, the assistant is told it is
there, and it decides to open it like any other operation. `product` is a new
conversation's, as on the plain message route.

schema.title: Response Say With A File Api Chat Upload Post

get.description:
One conversation, as a transcript plus whatever answers it has produced.

The stored messages are LangChain's, tool calls included, because the agent
resumes from them. What comes back here is the readable half of that -- who
said what -- because a person scrolling their own conversation has no use
for a serialised tool call.

`running` is read before the conversation is loaded (plan 031): a turn
that ends in between comes back saved and still reported, which the
page's next check corrects. Read after, a slow `answers_for` let a turn
end unseen, and the page drew a transcript without it, and no turn.

Opening it is using it: its `kept_until` starts again from now (plan 033).
A conversation whose questionnaire was deleted opens with `answers` null.

schema.title: Response Get Conversation Api Chat  Conversation Id  Get

delete.description:
Delete one of the caller's conversations, a deleted product's too. Its questionnaire and answers stay.

Not while a turn is running in it: 409 `conversation_busy` (plan 031).

schema.title: Response Forget Conversation Api Chat  Conversation Id  Delete

post.description:
Refused unless it is the conversation's own product: a chat's product is fixed once it starts.

Another product is 409 `product_locked` (TD-040); another team's is 404 `product_not_found` first.
A deleted product's chat is 409 `product_deleted` (plan 027). Kept so a page opened before the
change, or a script, is told why rather than finding no route.

schema.title: Response Choose Chat Product Api Chat  Conversation Id  Product Post

the answers ambiguous to match back.
